chains.summary: Seeing his own people, Arjuna is overcome and his limbs fail. He drops the bow and sits down in grief. He cannot tell which course is better. Confused about what is right, he asks to be taught.
chains.title: Arjuna's collapse

verses.m: Arjuna said: Krishna, when I see my own people standing here, eager to fight, I am overcome with pity and sorrow.
verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचकृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत् । दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥

verses.m: My limbs give way, my mouth is parched, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.
verses.sa: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥

verses.m: Sanjaya said: Having spoken this on the battlefield, Arjuna sank down on the seat of the chariot, letting fall his bow and arrows, his mind overwhelmed by grief.
verses.sa: सञ्जय उवाचएवमुक्त्वाऽर्जुनः संख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् । विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ॥

chains.summary: Without knowing there is no trust. Without trust there is no love. Without love devotion does not hold. No one finds rest without contentment. A boat does not move without water.
chains.title: Knowing, trust, love

verses.m: Without knowing his greatness, no trust forms; without trust, no love; and without love, devotion is not firm, just as, king of birds, oil does not stay on water.
verses.sa: जानें बिनु न होइ परतीती। बिनु परतीति होइ नहिं प्रीती॥ प्रीति बिना नहिं भगति दिढ़ाई। जिमि खगपति जल कै चिकनाई ॥

verses.m: Can anyone find rest without natural contentment, friend? Can a boat move without water, though you strain and wear yourself out with a million efforts?
verses.sa: कोउ बिश्राम कि पाव तात सहज संतोष बिनु। चलै कि जल बिनु नाव कोटि जतन पचि पचि मरिअ ॥

verses.m: Valour and patience are the wheels of that chariot; truth and good conduct are its firm flag and banner. Strength, discernment, self-control and kindness to others are its horses, yoked with the reins of forgiveness, compassion and evenness of mind.
verses.sa: सौरज धीरज तेहि रथ चाका। सत्य सील दृढ़ ध्वजा पताका॥ बल बिबेक दम परहित घोरे। छमा कृपा समता रजु जोरे ॥

verses.m: Delusion is the root of all diseases, and from it spring many pains. Desire is the wind, greed the endless phlegm, and anger the bile that keeps the chest burning.
verses.sa: मोह सकल ब्याधिन्ह कर मूला। तिन्ह ते पुनि उपजहिं बहु सूला॥ काम बात कफ लोभ अपारा। क्रोध पित्त नित छाती जारा ॥

verses.m: Possessiveness is ringworm and envy is the itch; the swings of elation and dejection are throat ailments. The burning you feel at another's happiness is consumption, and malice and a crooked mind are leprosy.
verses.sa: ममता दादु कंडु इरषाई। हरष बिषाद गरह बहुताई॥ पर सुख देखि जरनि सोइ छई। कुष्ट दुष्टता मन कुटिलई ॥

depicts.m: Knowing you as the Unborn, someone afraid comes to you for refuge: Rudra, with that kind, southern face of yours, protect me always.
depicts.sa: अजात इत्येवं कश्चिद्भीरुः प्रपद्यते । रुद्र यत्ते दक्षिणं मुखं तेन मां पाहि नित्यम् ॥

depicts.m: He who first brings forth Brahma and hands him the Vedas: to that God, who lights up the understanding of the self, I, longing for freedom, go for refuge.
depicts.sa: यो ब्रह्माणं विदधाति पूर्वं यो वै वेदांश्च प्रहिणोति तस्मै । तं ह देवं आत्मबुद्धिप्रकाशं मुमुक्षुर्वै शरणमहं प्रपद्ये ॥
depicts.why: Names first person longing to be free going for refuge.

depicts.m: Krishna, please cut away this doubt of mine completely. No one but you can remove it.
depicts.sa: एतन्मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः । त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता न ह्युपपद्यते ॥

depicts.m: In such a world, what use is the enjoyment of desires, when one who feeds on them is seen to return here again and again? Please lift me out. In this world I am like a frog in a dark well. Sir, you are my way, you are my way.
depicts.sa: सोऽहमित्येतद्विधेऽस्मिन्संसारे किं कामोपभोगैर्यैरेवाश्रितस्यासकृदिहावर्तनं दृश्यत इत्युद्धर्तुमर्हसीत्यन्धोदपानस्थो भेक इवाहमस्मिन्संसारे भगवंस्त्वं नो गतिस्त्वं नो गतिः ॥
depicts.why: Names you as my way, my way.

gloss: Handing oneself over is Arjuna's first move as a student and Krishna's last word, and Rama's vow to Vibhishana.

hero.m: Take refuge in Him alone with your whole being, Bharata. By His grace you will attain supreme peace and the eternal abode.
hero.sa: तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत । तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम् ॥

loci.m: Take refuge in Him alone with your whole being, Bharata. By His grace you will attain supreme peace and the eternal abode.
loci.sa: तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत । तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम् ॥

loci.m: This divine power of mine, made of the three qualities, is very hard to get past. Those who take refuge in me alone cross beyond it.
loci.sa: दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया । मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते ॥

loci.m: Whoever comes to me even once and says 'I am yours', asking for shelter, I give freedom from fear, from every being. This is my vow.
loci.sa: सकृदेव प्रपन्नाय तवास्मीति च याचते। अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो ददाम्येतद्ब्रतं मम॥

practices.m: Whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, that offering of love from the pure-hearted I accept.
practices.sa: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति । तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः ॥
practices.why: Shows devotion as what makes the gift.

practices.m: Ocean of compassion, Ganapati: may your radiance, which the whole world worships, by its own power quickly guard our minds, day and night, from wrong action, and urge them to good action. Blessed one, with Siddhi at your left side, we bow to you.
practices.sa: भर्गो विश्वसमर्चितं यदिह ते ह्यास्ते दयासागर ! तन्नो बुद्धिमहर्निशं गणपते ! शक्तचा स्वया सत्वरम । संरक्ष्यासत एव कर्मनिवहात् सत्कर्मणि प्रेरयेत् सियाऽलङ्कृतवामपार्श्व ! भगवस्त्वां सन्नमामो वयमा ॥

practices.m: Provisions for the wilderness of life, medicine that cuts the bonds of the world, rescue from sorrow and grief: the two syllables 'Ha-ri'.
Madhava is the father and the mother of all beings. Go to him for refuge, best of the Kurus; he is the refuge.
practices.sa: सर्वेषामेव भूतानां पिता माता च माधवः / गच्छध्वमेनं शरणं शरण्यं कौरवर्षभाः

practices.m: Fair as the jasmine and the moon, beloved of Uma, home of compassion, who loves the lowly: may the destroyer of Kama show me grace.
practices.sa: कुंद इंदु सम देह उमा रमन करुना अयन। जाहि दीन पर नेह करउ कृपा मर्दन मयन ॥
practices.why: Shows an opening prayer for grace.

practices.m: Tulsi says: if you want light both inside and outside, place the name of Ram like a jewelled lamp on the threshold of your tongue.
practices.sa: राम नाम मनिदीप धरु जीह देहरीं द्वार। तुलसी भीतर बाहेरहुँ जौं चाहसि उजिआर ॥
practices.why: Shows the name kept at the threshold of the tongue.

practices.m: Said with love or without it, even in irritation or laziness, repeating the name brings good in all ten directions. Remembering that name, I bow my head to Raghunath and begin his story.
practices.sa: भायँ कुभायँ अनख आलस हूँ। नाम जपत मंगल दिसि दसहूँ॥ सुमिरि सो नाम राम गुन गाथा। करउँ नाइ रघुनाथहि माथा ॥॥
practices.why: Saying the name as one is.

practices.m: Dweller in the shrine of devotees' hearts, all-pervading one, we come to you alone for refuge. Do now, divine Shambhu, whatever will quickly bring us good here.
practices.sa: विहारिन् ! विभो ! भक्तचेतोनिकेते शरण्यं किलैकान्ततस्त्वां व्रजामः । यथा नो भवेदत्र कल्याणमाशु तदेवाधुना देव ! शम्भो ! विधेहि ॥

stories.l: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.
stories.s: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.
stories.t: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness

stories.l: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.
stories.s: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all action, warns that ego will only trip him, tells him to reflect fully and then choose, and finally to take refuge in him alone and not grieve.

stories.l: When everything you knew is underwater, you have not been forgotten; you are being held.
stories.s: At the end of an age, the sage Markandeya drifts alone over a flooded world and sees a radiant child on a banyan branch. The child draws him inside his body, where he sees all the worlds, then asks if he has been resting, tired. Narayana explains he showed himself because he saw Markandeya's distress. Markandeya tells the Pandavas that this child is Krishna, sitting with them.
stories.t: Markandeya and the child on the banyan leaf

stories.l: Forgiveness can mean going first to the person who hurt you and putting them at ease.
stories.s: Bharat walks barefoot to Chitrakoot and falls at Ram's feet; Ram lifts him into his arms. Ram learns his father has died and grieves. When the queens arrive, Ram goes first to Kaikeyi, who caused it all, falls at her feet and comforts her, blaming no one.
